_comment: The cross-app import graph for the dev-lane apps, enforced by imports.py.
An app may reference another only when it is listed in may_import.
Adding an arrow is a design decision -- it records that two apps are now
coupled. Removing one is a promise the coupling is gone.
Every app in ops/devlane/ must appear here, and every app named here must
exist. A new app therefore cannot land without declaring its edges, which
is the point: the graph cannot drift while nobody is looking.
task -> telemetry: run.py loads telemetry/breaker.py by path to
supervise a dispatched agent. It was added when the task app landed,
by this check refusing the merge until it was declared.
dispatch -> task, dispatch -> harness: dispatch is the composition app
the §Dispatch launcher moved to (PR #61), so it may depend DOWNWARD on
both -- task for the jobs.json registry it reads by path, harness for
isolation.py/wires.py it loads to run an agent. task -> harness stays
forbidden: the launcher no longer lives in task, so that edge is gone
rather than allowed. The reverse (harness -> task) would be a cycle.
dispatch -> telemetry: launch.py loads telemetry/usage.py by path at close to
record session.spend from the harness's own store (U5, 2026-08-30). One
reader for the report and the record, so the two never disagree.
